_comment: The task file format is implemented twice — Sources/ToDoCore/TaskItem.swift
and mcp-server/taskfile.js — because the Swift app and the MCP server both
read and write the same folder. Two independent implementations of one
format WILL drift; this file is what catches it.
mcp-server/test/conformance.test.js assert against these exact cases.
Change parsing behaviour in either language and you must add or update a
case here — then run BOTH suites:
Every case below that is marked with a `regression` note is a real bug

times.regression: Swift's DateFormatter path returned nil, so a hand-typed '3pm' showed as a scheduled 3pm item to the MCP server and as an unscheduled to-do in the app.

times.note: minutes must be exactly two digits

times.regression: Swift used Int(parts[1].prefix(2)) and read this as 9:00; JS rejected it.

dates.regression: JS only checked the yyyy-MM-dd shape, so this passed there and rolled into March; Swift's non-lenient DateFormatter rejected it.

slugs.regression: Swift used Character.isLetter, which accepts non-ASCII letters, so the two sides generated different filenames for the same title. Both are now ASCII-only.

slugs.input: This title is definitely much longer than the forty character cap
slugs.note: hard cap at 40 characters, mid-word if need be

files.name: full-meeting
files.note: The everyday shape: every known key present.

expected.title: Crimsafe x Aircall x BAC Catchup
expected.body:
Items to discuss:
- Automatic contact creation
- Phone number formatting

files.name: minimal-task
files.note: An unscheduled to-do — no kind, no times, no link, no body.

files.name: unknown-keys-preserved
files.note: Comments, blank lines, and keys neither side knows must survive a round-trip byte-for-byte. `source` is written by the MCP server and is deliberately unknown to Swift.

files.name: no-frontmatter
files.note: A plain markdown file dropped into Tasks/. Must degrade to a filename-titled task, never be skipped or destroyed.

files.name: bad-values
files.note: Every value that can be wrong, is. Nothing here may throw; each bad field independently falls back. Its `created` is midday UTC on purpose: the invalid date falls back to the creation day in LOCAL time, and midday keeps that the same calendar day everywhere from UTC-12 to UTC+11.

files.name: colon-in-values
files.note: Only the FIRST colon separates key from value — titles and links routinely contain more.

files.name: crlf-line-endings
files.note: A file saved by a Windows-ish editor still has to parse.
